newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended much lower on Thursday as weaker bund futures at the open pushed guilder-bonds down and prices dipped further after the release of fresh economic data from the U.S. in late afternoon.

Dealers said the rise of the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management index to 54.0 in December from 52.7 in the previous month was in line with expectations, but the inflation component in the index worried the market.
The Price component in the index jumped to 51.5 from 45.9.
"This was not a good signal to the market," said one dealer, adding March bund futures dipped below 100 afterwards.
The March bund futures opened at 100.33 this morning, after closing at 100.79 during the last session in 1996.
At 1645 GMT those contracts were trading at 99.52.
The September 2001 bonds slipped to 116.06/16, with a bid yield of 4.83 percent versus 116.92/02 on Monday, December 30.
The January 2023 bonds fell to 110.16/36, with a bid yield of 6.67 percent versus 112.76/96 and a 6.47 percent yield on Monday.
Dealers were divided on the announcement of the new Dutch tender on Janaury 17, 1997. Some expected an issue in the 2001 or 2002 area, while others opted for a new ten-year issue.
